reasoning_traces.think:
The foundational structure of behavior emerges from four independent causal factors—S (stimulus), H (heredity), T (training), and P (purpose)—as posited by Purposive Behaviorism. These elements form a vector space of behavioral influence, each contributing distinct dimensions to action selection. The stimulus-response paradigm (S1 → R) is extended to include a gestalt expectation layer (E) that introduces uncertainty (U), triggering either direct response or adjustmental behavior (B). This process iterates through reinforcement cycles (S1 → B → S2), where each iteration refines the organism’s internal model of environmental stimuli. The inclusion of P allows for goal-directed behavior, distinguishing this framework from earlier paradigms like Structuralism and Spearmanism. The failure mode occurs when U is too high, causing erratic behavior, or when P is misaligned with S/H/T, resulting in maladaptive responses.
